clue.text: Seat Rex used until now

parts.note: a sofa is a seat for several people
Rex is Latin for king, abbreviated R as on coins and royal signatures

explanation.surface: A king's chair has been in use right up to the present.
explanation.walkthrough: 'used' is only a link here. R for Rex (king) is a standard crossword abbreviation.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means up to this point in time, the same as hitherto.

clue.text: Readily imbibing a litre in bar

indicators.note: imbibing means drinking in, so one word takes the following letters inside it

parts.note: readily, as in 'would as soon do it', means willingly or soon

explanation.surface: Someone in a pub happily downs a litre of drink.
explanation.walkthrough: 'imbibing' puts A and L inside SOON, which comes from 'Readily' in the sense of willingly.
explanation.definitionFit: A saloon is a bar or lounge in a pub, or a drinking house in the Wild West.

clue.text: Gourmand's intention to take kitchen waste

parts.note: a gourmand, a greedy eater, is a pig, and the possessive gives the S
a will is a firm intention or wish

explanation.surface: A greedy eater sets out to grab the leftovers from the kitchen.
explanation.walkthrough: Read 'Gourmand's intention' as a pig's will.
explanation.definitionFit: Scraps and leftover food fed to farm animals are known by this name.

clue.text: Refuse to accept increasing weakness

definitions.meaning: to turn down an offer or invitation politely
a gradual falling off in strength or health

explanation.surface: Someone will not admit that they are growing steadily feebler.
explanation.definitionFit: As a verb it means turn down an offer; as a noun it means a gradual deterioration in strength.

clue.text: He produced furniture to another's design

indicators.note: a design is a plan or arrangement, so the letters of the word before it are arranged anew

explanation.surface: A cabinetmaker builds pieces following someone else's plans.
explanation.walkthrough: 'design' rearranges the letters of 'another's', including the S of the possessive; 'to' is a link. Thomas Sheraton was an 18th-century English furniture designer.
explanation.definitionFit: Thomas Sheraton was a celebrated Georgian cabinetmaker whose name became a furniture style.

clue.text: Severely rebuked for having worn ill-fitting shoes?

definitions.meaning: criticised fiercely, as with a scathing attack
tight shoes rub the feet and raise sore bubbles on the skin

explanation.surface: Someone was told off harshly for squeezing into shoes that did not fit.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags that the second definition is a consequence of the shoes, not a synonym.
explanation.definitionFit: Figuratively the word means harshly criticised; literally it describes skin covered in sore swellings, as from rubbing footwear.

clue.text: Safe bond I converted in good faith

indicators.note: converted means changed in form, so these letters are changed into a new order

explanation.surface: A reliable investment certificate is exchanged honestly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'converted' rearranges SAFE, BOND and I; 'in' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: The Latin phrase names sincerity and honest intention, especially as credentials.

clue.text: Child ailing as result of cold

parts.note: ailing means sick or unwell

explanation.surface: A youngster falls sick after catching a cold.
explanation.walkthrough: 'as result of' is a link joining the wordplay to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A chill is a feverish cold, or simply coldness in the air.

clue.text: Heated conflict supported by Malta

indicators.note: in a down clue a piece supported by another has that other piece written beneath it

parts.note: a war is an armed conflict
M is the international vehicle registration code for Malta

explanation.surface: A fierce war receives backing from Malta.
explanation.walkthrough: 'supported by' places M below WAR in the down light.
explanation.definitionFit: Something heated has been made hot or at least not cold.

clue.text: Bacchanal provides many with excitement

parts.note: C is the Roman numeral for a hundred, so it stands for many
arousal is a state of excitement or stimulation

explanation.surface: A drunken party gives plenty of people a thrill.
explanation.walkthrough: 'provides' is a link. Many = C (100 in Roman numerals) is a crossword convention.
explanation.definitionFit: A bacchanal is a drunken revel, named after Bacchus, god of wine, just as a carousal is.

clue.text: Stop to apprehend a law-breaker

definitions.meaning: to halt or check something, as in stopping a decline
to take a suspect into police custody

explanation.surface: A police officer halts to seize a criminal.
explanation.definitionFit: To halt is one sense of the verb; detaining a suspect in custody is the other.

clue.text: In the meantime Tories are in opposition

indicators.note: In tells the solver the letters sit inside the following word

explanation.surface: Meanwhile the Conservative Party sits on the opposition benches.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters sit inside 'meantime'; 'the' and 'Tories are' only complete the surface. The definition works as a prefix-like adjective meaning against.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means against, opposed to something.

clue.text: Gossip about retired medic? Forget it!

indicators.note: about means around, so one word goes around the other

parts.note: to natter is to chat or gossip

indicators.note: retired means drawn back, so the word for medic is read backwards

parts.note: MO, medical officer, is an army doctor

explanation.surface: People chatter about a doctor who has stopped working, then say it doesn't matter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'retired' looks like a doctor who has stopped working; it means the medic is turned round, and 'about' wraps the gossip word around it. A medical officer is an army doctor.
explanation.definitionFit: Both are dismissive phrases telling someone the issue is unimportant.

clue.text: Unwanted interference results in angry words

definitions.meaning: signals leaking between telephone or radio channels
a cross exchange of talk

explanation.surface: Meddling leads to a heated argument.
explanation.walkthrough: 'results in' is only a link between the two definitions.
explanation.definitionFit: Technically it is signal leakage between circuits; read as two words it is talk that is cross, that is angry.

clue.text: Chairman goes to French island to write short sketch

parts.note: a professor holds a university chair, so a chairman can be a prof
ile is the French word for island

explanation.surface: A company head travels to an island in France to draft a brief outline.
explanation.walkthrough: 'goes to' and 'to' are links. 'Chairman' looks like a company head; it is a professor holding a chair.
explanation.definitionFit: As a verb it means to write a brief biographical account of someone.

clue.text: Fellow criminal is unimpaired

parts.note: lawless means acting outside the law, criminal

explanation.surface: Another crook gets off without a scratch.
explanation.walkthrough: 'is' is a link between wordplay and definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Something without defects or blemishes is perfect and undamaged.

clue.text: Bell makes a boob

definitions.meaning: something that rings loudly, a thing that clangs
an embarrassing mistake or gaffe

explanation.surface: A bell rings out a blunder.
explanation.walkthrough: 'makes' is a link. To drop one is British slang for making an embarrassing blunder.
explanation.definitionFit: Literally something that rings with a metallic sound; in British slang a glaring mistake.

clue.text: Lone dame ordered a drink

indicators.note: ordered means arranged, so these letters are put into a new order

explanation.surface: A solitary lady asked for a beverage.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ordered' looks like the dame placing an order at a bar; it rearranges LONE and DAME.
explanation.definitionFit: It is a soft drink flavoured with citrus juice.

clue.text: Colour to paint borders in study?

indicators.note: in places one word inside another

parts.note: to con is to study or learn by heart
rims are edges or borders

explanation.surface: A decorator wonders what shade to use for the edges of a study.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to paint' completes the surface only. CON for study is an old verb meaning to pore over.
explanation.definitionFit: Crimson is a deep red, a kind of hue.

clue.text: Manxman, maybe, admits to character defamation

parts.note: someone who admits to a fault begins by saying I
slander is spoken defamation of a person's character

explanation.surface: A man from the Isle of Man confesses to badmouthing people.
explanation.walkthrough: The confession 'I slander' is what someone who admits to character defamation says. A Manxman is from the Isle of Man, an island in the Irish Sea.
explanation.definitionFit: A Manxman lives on an island, so he is one example of a resident of such a place.

clue.text: Peach bowl

definitions.meaning: an attractive person, a looker
a shallow vessel for serving food

explanation.surface: A peach sits in a fruit bowl.
explanation.walkthrough: Both words are nouns: 'Peach' for a good-looking person, not the fruit.
explanation.definitionFit: Slang for a good-looking person; also a serving vessel or plate.

clue.text: Such a melon has a strong scent

definitions.meaning: a type of melon with a sweet fragrant flesh
a heavy perfume, originally from a deer gland

explanation.surface: A certain melon gives off a powerful smell.
explanation.walkthrough: 'has' is a link between the two definitions.
explanation.definitionFit: It names a variety of sweet-smelling melon and also a pungent perfume base from the musk deer.

clue.text: Sunglasses of various hues

definitions.meaning: dark glasses, in informal speech
different gradations of a colour

explanation.surface: Sunglasses come in assorted colours.
explanation.walkthrough: 'of' is a link between the two definitions.
explanation.definitionFit: Slang for dark glasses; also tints or tones of colour.

clue.text: In the money after winning hand at poker

definitions.meaning: having plenty of cash, well off
five cards all of one suit

explanation.surface: A gambler is rich after a winning deal at the card table.
explanation.walkthrough: 'after' is a link between the two definitions.
explanation.definitionFit: Informally it means well supplied with cash; in poker it is a hand of five cards of the same suit.

clue.text: Stands to get theatre seats

definitions.meaning: booths or market tables for selling goods
seats on the ground floor of a theatre

explanation.surface: People queue at the box office to buy good seats.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to get' is a link. In British theatres this name is used for the ground-floor seating, called the orchestra in the US.
explanation.definitionFit: Booths at a market are stands; in a British theatre the term covers the ground-floor seats.

clue.text: Males score intellectually

parts.note: men are males
a tally is a score or count

explanation.surface: Men keep score using their brains.
explanation.definitionFit: The adverb means in terms of the mind or thinking.

clue.text: Stop proceedings when it's stuffy

definitions.meaning: to bring a meeting or session to an end
airless and humid, as weather can be

explanation.surface: A meeting is ended because the room is airless.
explanation.walkthrough: 'when it's' is a link between the two definitions.
explanation.definitionFit: As a verb it means to end business; as an adjective it means airless and muggy.

clue.text: Endorses a scheme to promote traffic awareness

indicators.note: to scheme is to plan or arrange, so these letters are arranged afresh

explanation.surface: A council backs a plan to make drivers more alert.
explanation.walkthrough: 'scheme' rearranges ENDORSES and A; 'to promote' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means a driver's or pedestrian's instinct for safe behaviour among vehicles.
